title: Unused, duplicated and overlapping indexes: the tax they charge on writes

videos.script: Every index on a table is a promise the database keeps on every write. {{promise}} Insert one order into a table with nine indexes, and the server writes ten things. It does that whether anybody ever reads the other nine or not. {{fanout}} Over three years of migrations, indexes pile up like that. One for a screen, one for a report, one somebody added twice without noticing. {{migrations}} Nobody removes them, because removing an index feels risky and keeping one feels free. It is not free. {{tax}} In this lesson you build seven of those leftovers on the market database, and you measure what they cost. Orders a second, and the bytes of log each order writes. {{measure}} Then you find which ones are dead weight. The ones no query has read, with the four reasons that zero can lie. {{unused}} The ones that are exact copies of another index. {{duplicates}} And the ones whose columns are the start of a longer index, which answers the same questions. {{overlap}} Finally you drop them the safe way, without locking the table and with the way back written down. Then you measure again. {{drop}} By the end, a list of indexes will read to you like a list of bills, and you will know which ones to stop paying. {{title}}
